claims.text: Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy in multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
Machine-learning algorithms can improve determination of volume change and dense-fluid heat capacity in multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
The proposed machine-learning algorithms would be trained on a large dataset of high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy is the structural or thermodynamic mediator through which the intervention acts.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns reflecting the thermodynamic principles governing high-entropy alloys at high temperatures.
Kinetic principles govern the targeted high-temperature behavior and can be captured by the machine-learning algorithms.
The intervention will improve predictive accuracy relative to currently used experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve efficiency relative to currently used experimental and computational methods.
Experimental methods and computational approaches are currently used to determine thermodynamic behavior in multicomponent alloys.
Performance of the proposed approach is limited by the quality of its training dataset.
Performance of the proposed approach is limited by the size of its training dataset.
Performance of the proposed approach is limited by the complexity of the material system.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of the training data and the machine-learning algorithms.
Comparison against high-temperature experimental measurements can test predictions of transition temperature, fusion properties, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
